title: Creamy Vanilla Pudding
summary: A smooth, creamy stovetop vanilla pudding thickened with cornflour and egg yolks and chilled until set.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Slurry
steps.text: in the large bowl whisk the cornflour into 60 ml of the cold milk until completely smooth, then whisk in the yolks. Mixing the starch with cold milk first stops lumps.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: warm the rest of the milk with the sugar and salt until steaming and small bubbles appear at the edge.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: pour the hot milk slowly into the yolk mixture, whisking all the time, then pour everything back into the pan. Adding the hot milk slowly warms the yolks without scrambling them.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: whisk over medium heat until it thickens and the first bubbles break the surface, then keep whisking 1 min; it should read 82 °C or more. Cornflour only thickens fully once it bubbles.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: off the heat, whisk in the butter and vanilla, then press through the sieve.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: divide between the bowls, lay baking paper on the surface and chill 3 h. Stir briefly before serving. Paper on the surface stops a skin forming.

tips: A common mistake is stopping too early; the pudding must bubble, or it will go runny as it cools.
Whisk all the time, reaching into the corners of the pan.
Serve with whipped cream or fresh berries.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Do not freeze.
